findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is optional/null, so destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can produce `undefined`. The subsequent direct access to `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws for a Google Meet event without a destination calendar, precisely the case this fallback is meant to handle. This prevents the booking from being created instead of falling back to Cal Video; guard the value or use optional chaining.

findings.title: The selected destination calendar is not passed to calendar providers
findings.body: Although `createEvent` accepts `externalId` and `EventManager` supplies each destination's ID, this call invokes the provider with only the complete `CalendarEvent` array and the credential ID. Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV currently select `destinationCalendar[0]`, so when iterating a second collective host they attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar (often with an unauthorized credential). The `externalId` is only copied into the resulting reference later and does not affect where the event is created. Pass the selected destination through to the provider, or have every provider select the entry matching the credential/target.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are discarded when the first host has no destination calendar
findings.body: The initial event value is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The collective-host calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which silently does nothing for that case. A collective booking where another host has a calendar but the organizer does not therefore has no destination calendars and no host calendar event is created. Initialize this field as an empty array or assign a new array when adding host calendars.

findings.title: Only the first collective destination is persisted on the booking
findings.body: The booking write connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so all secondary host destination calendars are lost once the request completes. Deferred scheduling paths such as confirmation and payment webhooks rebuild their `CalendarEvent` from the singular `booking.destinationCalendar` and consequently create an event only for the main host. Persist all destination-calendar selections (or reliably reconstruct them from the collective hosts) before supporting deferred collective bookings.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credential ID
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now sets `credentialId` to `undefined` for every non-calendar result. Dedicated video results previously retained `result.credentialId`; removing it creates video BookingReferences without the credential needed to update or delete the meeting. For example, the cancellation handler only deletes a video meeting when its reference has a credential ID, leaving these meetings orphaned. Preserve `result.credentialId` for video results.

findings.title: Location updates create calendar references without calendar or credential identifiers
findings.body: `updateLocation` now copies `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` into new references, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not populate either field in its returned EventResult. Every calendar reference appended by the location-update flow will therefore have no external calendar ID or credential ID. Later updates/cancellations cannot target the original event and may fall back to all connected calendars. Return the input credential/calendar identifiers from `updateEvent`, or derive them from the source reference before writing the new one.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback can never select a destination calendar
findings.body: The fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, then searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value. Since calendar IDs are strings, it always produces `undefined`. Updates then send an undefined `calendarId`, while the analogous delete logic at line 317 falls back to `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar. Existing references without an externalCalendarId will fail updates or delete the wrong calendar event; choose an actual destination fallback, such as the entry associated with the credential.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only one calendar reference per occurrence
findings.body: For each recurring occurrence this code uses `.find(...)` to select the first calendar reference, then invokes deletion through every calendar credential. With multiple collective-host references, the remaining references are never selected with their own credential and calendar ID; the outer reference loop merely repeats the same first-reference work. Secondary host events remain on their calendars after cancelling all remaining occurrences. Iterate every occurrence reference and resolve/use that reference's credential ID.

findings.title: Reschedule cleanup collapses multiple host credentials of the same integration
findings.body: The cleanup map is keyed only by integration type, so multiple collective references such as two `google_calendar` host calendars are all deleted using whichever credential was last inserted for that type. A host credential normally cannot delete another host's calendar event; Google treats a 404 as a successful delete here, so the failure can be silent and leave the old event behind. Resolve the credential by each BookingReference's `credentialId` rather than by its type.

findings.title: Organization slug creation condition was inverted
findings.body: This changes slug persistence from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations no longer receive the slug that was validated and used to create the domain, making their organization URL unavailable. With billing enabled, it also assigns the slug immediately instead of retaining it as `requestedSlug`, bypassing the previous approval behavior. This unrelated inversion should be reverted.

findings.title: The public booking webhook payload changes destinationCalendar shape without compatibility handling
findings.body: CalendarEvent is serialized into booking webhook payloads, as demonstrated by the webhook E2E test. Changing `destinationCalendar` from an object/null to an array changes the JSON contract for every existing webhook consumer that reads fields such as `destinationCalendar.externalId` or expects null. The PR provides no payload versioning, compatibility field, or migration documentation, so consumers will break when hosts have a destination calendar.

findings.title: No automated test covers the multi-destination collective lifecycle
findings.body: The PR adds creation, update, and cancellation paths for multiple destination calendars but does not test a collective booking with distinct host credentials/calendars. A test should verify that each provider receives its own selected calendar and that the resulting references allow reschedule and cancellation to update/delete every host event. The existing webhook expectation change only checks an empty-array payload and would not detect the first-destination and missing-reference regressions.
